 THE TIMES OF INDIA | Oct 30, 2026, 14:58:16 IST SUMMARY India vs New Zealand Live Score: New Zealand face another stern test of their bowling attack as they take on India in the fourth T20I at Eden Park, Auckland, on Friday, October 30. India have already secured an unassailable 3-0 lead in the five-match series after producing three successful run chases, including a commanding victory in Wellington, where they chased down 199 in just 13.2 overs. 
 The defending T20 World Cup champions have continued to showcase their explosive batting depth, with Abhishek Sharma and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi leading the charge in the previous match. Their aggressive approach has left New Zealand searching for answers, particularly after the hosts' seamers conceded runs at an economy rate of 12.85 against India in T20Is this year. 
 Mitchell Santner's side will need to find a way to contain India's top order if they are to prevent a series whitewash. The challenge is made tougher by the absence of injured fast bowlers Lockie Ferguson and Matt Henry. Nathan Smith is expected to return after missing the third T20I, while Kyle Jamieson is set to feature in the Ford Trophy. 
 Eden Park's compact straight boundaries could offer another high-scoring contest, although the larger square boundaries and rectangular playing area will require smart bowling plans and field placements. 
 India, meanwhile, could use the remaining matches to rotate their squad after sealing the series. Mayank Yadav may get another opportunity, while Kuldeep Yadav, Varun Chakravarthy and Shivam Dube are yet to feature. 
 The fourth T20I offers New Zealand a chance to respond, but India's batting firepower makes them formidable opponents. Commentary

This is something you don't associate with New Zealand. Duffy drags it shorter and fires it outside off, Abhishek hangs back and pulls it away over mid-wicket. Smith charges in too hard to his right, loses his footing, slides past the ball and concedes four.

He did all the hard work, but just couldn't get the hold of it. Pitched up and wide outside off, Abhishek steps forward, looking to clear the infield, but the bat twists in his grip and he slices it off the toe end over mid off. Santner gives chase from the inner ring, running over his left shoulder. He keeps himself side-on to his left and dives near long off, only for the ball to burst through his hands. Two runs taken.

The Kiwis are right over the Men in Blue now. Jacob goes full and on the leg stump line, Kishan drops to one knee, looking to whip it away, but shuts the bat face too early in the attempt. Hence, the ball takes the cue end of the bat and bobbles back to the bowler. Jacob Duffy keeps his cool, backtracks a bit and takes a simple return catch with a reverse cup. India are 4/2, chasing 260.

The extra bounce does the trick for Duffy. He bangs it very short on top of the stumps, and extracts more bounce off the surface. Sanju backs away again to play the pull shot but the ball gets really big on him and he ends up spooning it off the top edge, over the keeper. Tim Seifert lurks under the swirling ball and takes a fine diving catch. India are 4/1, needing 256 runs.

Full from Duffy, swinging away from middle to off, Sanju backs away to make room, maintains his shape and lofts it over extra cover for an effortless boundary. India and Samson are off the mark in style!
 14:39 (IST) Oct 30 Welcome back to the chase! The umpires are back out in the middle, and so are the players of New Zealand. Sanju Samson is back out to open for India, alongside Abhishek Sharma. Jacob Duffy will get proceedings underway with the ball. Let's play...
 14:39 (IST) Oct 30 ... The Run Chase ...
 14:35 (IST) Oct 30 Listless from the bowlers - It's been a tough evening for the Indian bowlers, and barring Arshdeep Singh, no one else went for less than 10 runs an over. Mayank Yadav did well to pick up those 3 timely wickets, but not having that fifth proper bowling option really hurt India. In general, only Arshdeep showcased consistency, whereas Prince Yadav bowled a solid over at the death. But the likes of Nitish Kumar Reddy, Naman Dhir and even Axar Patel went for plenty. Nitish even bowled one over where he conceded 32 runs, and now the Indian batters have it all to do. Can Abhishek Sharma pull off another heist and give India the platform to gun down 260 runs? We shall find out soon. Stay tuned as the run chase is up next.
 14:32 (IST) Oct 30 Phillips goes ballistic - Glenn Phillips has been the most consistent batter in this series, and barring a rare failure in Match 3, he's been just untouchable. Tim Seifert fell early which has been the norm and Daryl Mitchell too fell after a quick start. Then came the partnership between Finn Allen and Phillips that got the Kiwis into a position of promise. Phillips looked in sublime form, but Allen fell and then so did Bevon Jacobs, leaving the hosts in a spot of bother. However, Michael Bracewell came in and just seized the opportunity, absolutely pummeling the Indian attack. Bracewell added 115 super-quick runs alongside Phillips, who then went on to score a fantastic century. New Zealand scored exactly 150 runs in the second half of their innings and now have a very good chance of winning a game in this series.
 14:27 (IST) Oct 30 Record-breaking total - What a showing with the bat from New Zealand, especially Glenn Phillips, and they have piled on a total of 259 runs on the board, which is the new record for T20Is here at Eden Park. However, the last time Kiwis broke a similar record here was against Australia, where they scored 243 runs, and Australia managed to chase it down, and you wouldn't put it past this Indian lineup either, so it's game on!

Full ball by Arshdeep, outside the off stump, Glenn Phillips gets underneath it properly and belts it over long off. It looked so, so effortless. Off comes the helmet, up goes the bat, and his teammates rise to salute a truly special innings.

 149 More Updates Load More India vs New Zealand Live Score: India have taken an unassailable 3-0 lead in the five-match T20I series against New Zealand, but the contest moves to a venue that could offer another fascinating batting spectacle. The fourth T20I will be played at Eden Park in Auckland on Friday, October 30, with the match scheduled to begin at 12:30 PM IST (8:00 PM local time).
India have made a habit of chasing down targets in this series. Their latest performance in Wellington was particularly emphatic, as they overhauled New Zealand's 198 for 3 in only 13.2 overs. Abhishek Sharma and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi provided the fireworks, reinforcing the depth and attacking intent of India's batting line-up. The team's Powerplay average of 85 in the series underlines how aggressively they have started their innings.
New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner knows his bowlers must come up with a different approach. The hosts have struggled to contain India's batters, with their seamers conceding at an economy rate of 12.85 in T20Is against India in 2026. Santner remains a key threat, having taken 30 T20I wickets against India, and is the only New Zealand bowler with an economy rate below 10 in this series.
The hosts have also suffered injury setbacks, with Lockie Ferguson and Matt Henry ruled out of the remaining T20Is. Nathan Smith is expected to return after missing the previous match with a minor niggle.
Eden Park's short straight boundaries could favour the big hitters, although bowlers will need to use the larger square boundaries intelligently. The venue has witnessed a successful T20I chase of 245, but its most recent international T20 match in March was dominated by bowlers.
With the series already decided, India could also experiment with their combinations. Mayank Yadav may return, while Kuldeep Yadav, Varun Chakravarthy and Shivam Dube are yet to play. New Zealand, meanwhile, will be desperate to avoid a 5-0 whitewash.
